title: Source invertibility for a specified pro-isomorphism of Milnor triangles
statement: Let C be a pretriangulated preadditive category with a zero object and additive integer shifts. Let F and G be inverse sequences with product fans PF and PG, and let distinguished Milnor triangles with first vertices X and Y be specified for these fans. Suppose a:F->G has backward successor maps b_n:G_(n+1)->F_n whose two composites with a are the two tower transitions. Every map u:X->Y which, together with the product map induced by a, commutes with the first arrows and the shifted boundary arrows of the specified triangles is an isomorphism.

proof.text: The product of the backward successor maps defines a reverse product map. Its two composites with the forward product map are the two tower shifts. Complete the reverse product square to a morphism of distinguished triangles. In each Milnor triangle the first arrow followed by tower shift equals the first arrow, and tower shift followed by the boundary equals the boundary: both follow from vanishing of consecutive composites with one minus tower shift. Thus the two composite triangle morphisms have the same first-arrow and boundary actions as the identity. Apply isIso_hom₁_of_comp to these four equations. This is the existing complete source proof, and it requires both displayed compatibilities of the given map u.

theorem isIso_of_proIso {X Y : C} {cX : X ⟶ PF.pt} {δX : PF.pt ⟶ X⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧} {cY : Y ⟶ PG.pt}
    {δY : PG.pt ⟶ Y⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧} (hX : Triangle.mk cX (𝟙 _ - towerShift hPF) δX ∈ distTriang C)
    (hY : Triangle.mk cY (𝟙 _ - towerShift hPG) δY ∈ distTriang C) (a : F ⟶ G)
    (b : ∀ n : ℕ, G.obj (op (n + 1)) ⟶ F.obj (op n))
    (hb₁ : ∀ n, b n ≫ a.app (op n) = G.map (homOfLE n.le_succ).op)
    (hb₂ : ∀ n, a.app (op (n + 1)) ≫ b n = F.map (homOfLE n.le_succ).op)
    (u : X ⟶ Y) (hu₁ : cX ≫ productTowerMap (PF := PF) hPG a = u ≫ cY)
    (hu₃ : δX ≫ u⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧' = productTowerMap (PF := PF) hPG a ≫ δY) : IsIso u
